## Purpose and runtime
Mimik is a Manifest V3 browser extension that records browser workflows into locally stored, editable step-by-step guides with screenshots. It targets Chrome, Firefox, and Edge; no application backend or account is required. Extension build/runtime configuration is rooted in `wxt.config.ts`, with TypeScript sources under `src/`.

## Extension entry points and process boundaries
The content script injects capture, replay, blur, and screenshot-facing behavior into recorded web pages: `src/entrypoints/content.ts`. The background service worker coordinates tabs, navigation, recording state, persisted-guide updates, deferred AI work, and narration: `src/entrypoints/background/index.ts`, `src/entrypoints/background/actor.ts`, `src/entrypoints/background/step-pipeline.ts`. UI surfaces are separate extension documents: side panel `src/entrypoints/sidepanel/index.tsx`, full-page library/editor `src/entrypoints/fullview/index.tsx`, plus offscreen audio support `src/entrypoints/offscreen/index.ts`.

## Capture pipeline
Capture is modeled as a state machine and session lifecycle, turning DOM events, input sessions, SPA/full navigation, and intercepted clicks into recordable steps: `src/core/capture/machine.ts`, `src/core/capture/session.ts`, `src/core/capture/events/handlers.ts`. DOM context and element metadata establish the target identity and human-readable fallback descriptions: `src/core/capture/dom/context.ts`, `src/core/capture/dom/element-meta.ts`, `src/core/capture/step-description.ts`. Content-side events cross the extension boundary through messaging utilities; background orchestration serializes them into the step pipeline: `src/lib/messaging.ts`, `src/lib/tab-messages.ts`, `src/entrypoints/background/step-pipeline.ts`.

## Visual capture and privacy controls
Screenshot rendering derives target geometry, highlights, zoom/cropping, and draw operations: `src/core/screenshot/render.ts`, `src/core/screenshot/geometry.ts`, `src/core/screenshot/draw.ts`. Privacy is applied as a first-class processing layer: regex scanning detects common sensitive values, while manual element selection and a manager/panel propagate redactions across applicable captures: `src/core/blur/scanner.ts`, `src/core/blur/element-picker.ts`, `src/core/blur/manager.ts`.

## Guides, editing, and replay
Guide data is locally persisted and manipulated through a guide service, block model, snapshots/versioning, and change messaging: `src/core/guides/db.ts`, `src/core/guides/service.ts`, `src/core/guides/snapshot-groups.ts`. The side panel supports active recording and guide editing; the full-view surface provides library, editor, search, and history-oriented workflows: `src/ui/sidepanel/App.tsx`, `src/ui/sidepanel/GuideEditor.tsx`, `src/ui/fullview/App.tsx`. “Guide Me” resolves recorded targets on a live page and overlays interaction guidance while tracking progression: `src/core/guideme/finder.ts`, `src/core/guideme/overlay.ts`, `src/core/guideme/session.ts`.

## Optional AI and voice services
AI descriptions use user-supplied OpenAI or Anthropic credentials, send lightweight DOM-derived text rather than screenshots, and are queued/deferred by the background worker: `src/core/capture/ai/provider.ts`, `src/core/capture/ai/description.ts`, `src/entrypoints/background/description-queue.ts`. Voice narration records audio via mic/offscreen hosts, gates and batches it, transcribes through OpenAI or Groq, then associates narration windows with captured steps: `src/lib/mic-recorder.ts`, `src/core/capture/voice/pipeline.ts`, `src/core/capture/voice/transcribe.ts`. API keys remain local but selected providers receive the opted-in text/audio.

## Export and delivery
Exports transform guide data and rendered assets client-side into PDF, DOCX, HTML, Markdown, GIF, and encoded video, then trigger browser downloads: `src/core/export/pdf-export.ts`, `src/core/export/video-export.ts`, `src/core/export/download.ts`. Full-view export preview/UI invokes those formats: `src/ui/fullview/ExportPreviewModal.tsx`. The only documented non-user-provider external fetch is favicon retrieval; all guide content and generated artifacts remain device-local.
